title: When to use print, when to use return
idea: TOOL: choose print to communicate with a person; choose return to pass a value to more code.

exercises.prompt: Your sub-plan's answer will be added to another number later. print or return?
options: return - the value must be reused
exercises.explanation: If more code needs the value, return it. Only a returned value can be combined with other numbers.

exercises.prompt: Your sub-plan just needs to display a greeting for the user. print or return?
options: print - it only needs to be seen
exercises.explanation: If the goal is only to show something to a person, print is enough. No value needs to travel onward.

exercises.prompt: A sub-plan computes a total that the main program will store and use again. Best choice?
options: print the total and forget it
exercises.explanation: The main program must reuse the total, so return it. Returning keeps the value usable.

exercises.prompt: A good rule of thumb: return the answer, and let the CALLER decide whether to print it.
exercises.explanation: Yes. If the sub-plan returns, the caller can print it, store it, or combine it - the caller stays in control.

exercises.prompt: Why is 'return the value, print in the caller' often better than printing inside the sub-plan?
options: It keeps the sub-plan reusable in more situations
exercises.explanation: A returning sub-plan works whether you want to print, store, or combine. Printing inside locks it to one use.

exercises.prompt: Match each goal to the right tool.

pairs.left: Show a message to the user
Pass a value into more math

exercises.explanation: print for people, return for more code. Matching the tool to the goal keeps your sub-plans clean.
area returns 15; the caller chooses to print it. The sub-plan computes, the caller decides what to do.

options: One that only prints its result
exercises.explanation: A returning sub-plan can be printed, stored, or combined. A print-only one can only ever show its result.

exercises.prompt: REVIEW: returning lets the caller use a value in which earlier tools?
options: math, comparisons, storing in variables - all of them
exercises.explanation: A returned value is a normal value: it works with arithmetic, comparisons, and assignment. That is the power.

exercises.prompt: If you are unsure, returning is usually the safer choice because the caller can still print it.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Returning keeps options open. If you only print, the value is gone and cannot be reused.
